question: To study the flow of blood in the systemic circulation, partially occlusive stents are placed in the pulmonary trunk of a physiological system while the pressure in the right atrium is monitored. A graph where the right atrial pressure is a function of venous return is plotted. Assuming all circulatory nerve reflexes are absent in the system, at what point on the diagram shown below will the arterial pressure be closest to the venous pressure?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Point I -> arterial pressure is closest to venous pressure -> 80% CHAIN: Point II -> arterial pressure is closest to venous pressure -> 90% CHAIN: Point III -> arterial pressure is closest to venous pressure -> 70% CHAIN: Point IV -> arterial pressure is closest to venous pressure -> 60% CHAIN: Point V -> arterial pressure is closest to venous pressure -> 80%
analysis: In a physiological system with partially occlusive stents in the pulmonary trunk and absent circulatory nerve reflexes, the point on the graph where arterial pressure is closest to venous pressure would be where the right atrial pressure curve intersects the x-axis (zero venous return). This is because at zero venous return, the arterial pressure would be closest to the venous pressure.
